items.title: TextHuman
items.description: Writing tools, local text editing and document import.
items.story:
TextHuman is a writing product that connects text editing, document import, accounts and subscription workflows. Its interface lets the writer choose a regional style, level of formality and perspective.

The application brings together a browser interface, Cloudflare Workers, PostgreSQL, Mercado Pago and transactional email. Document import handles PDF text layers and the XML inside DOCX and PPTX files.

The design challenge is to keep a configurable writing workflow approachable: choose the context, work with a document, compare the result and keep the text you need.

items.title: MyFather
items.story:
An educational web experience with Spanish and English lessons, activities, progress and reward logic.

Adult and supervised child experiences are distinct. Routine lessons do not require an external AI model; the architecture separates the public application from the private Worker and administrative operations.

items.title: SHIFT · TRAZA FIT
items.description: Work-integrated learning, from exploration to evidence.
items.story:
TRAZA FIT is a work-integrated learning project for the Tecmilenio SHIFT challenge. It turns workplace situations into guided practice, decisions, reflection and evidence.

The interface includes degree-specific pathways, a professional passport, activities and bilingual content. This interactive portfolio preview uses sample data and browser-local state.

items.title: SHIFT Control
items.description: An editorial control workspace for TRAZA.
items.story:
A separate control interface for creating, editing, publishing and targeting learning resources. The source includes content states, audiences, media, student-related modules and reports.

The portfolio preview lets visitors inspect the workflow using sample data; it is separate from institutional accounts and connected production controls.

items.title: TRAZA FIT · SHIFT
items.story:
TRAZA FIT translates a work-integrated learning idea into an interface with career pathways, guided activities and evidence collection. A software-development pathway can put the learner inside a checkout incident and ask them to reason about impact, risk and communication before making a decision.

The project separates the student experience from the editorial control workspace. Its React and TypeScript source includes resources, simulations, practices, surveys and bilingual content. The connected design uses a Worker and Supabase for protected operations.

The portfolio demonstration runs the existing local interface with sample data, so the experience can be explored without institutional credentials.

items.title: Atenea
items.description: A wearable interaction concept for gentle wake-up guidance.
items.story:
Atenea explores how a wearable assistant might pair gentle cues with encouraging guidance during a wake-up sequence. The concept focuses on interaction across the chest, shoulders and back, and on the way a person experiences each step.

The work is currently in planning and interaction design. The repository contains architecture questions, a component inventory, a roadmap and a decision log. Hardware selection and integration remain part of the development work.

The interactive study here lets visitors explore cue locations and a proposed sequence. It is a visual simulation of the idea, rather than a claim that working hardware has already been built.

items.title: NorthPeak
items.description: An incident workflow built around visible SQL.
items.story:
NorthPeak is a fictional manufacturing-company case study built to demonstrate a full business and systems analysis workflow: requirements, processes, implementation, data, testing and improvement.

The implementation uses Python and Flask, SQLite with visible raw SQL, a ticket queue, status history and a dashboard. Its documentation includes AS-IS and TO-BE process maps, a data model, test plans, defect tracking and a user manual. Excel export and Power BI integration are discussed as part of the reporting workflow.

The original test suite covers ticket creation, state transitions, history, aggregation and error handling. This browser preview recreates the ticket interaction using disposable sample data.

items.title: Argus AI
items.description: Streaming anomaly detection and rule-driven alert logging.
items.story:
Argus AI is a hackathon prototype that turns incoming demo telemetry into anomaly flags and logged response labels. Its loop is stream, detect, match a rule and record the proposed action.

The anomaly engine uses pure-Python exponentially weighted statistics: per-metric EWMA z-scores and an online Mahalanobis distance across a device’s metric set. The backend is FastAPI, with WebSocket updates and SQLite storage; the frontend combines JavaScript and charts.

A simulator and self-seeding fleet make the system explorable without physical sensors. Actions such as notify or shutdown are labels in the demo log; they do not control real equipment.

items.title: SmartLibrary
items.story:
SmartLibrary is a Java and NetBeans library-management project described in my original CV. It brings together object-oriented programming and a Swing interface.

Its workflow includes role-based access, CRUD operations, loans, returns, history and statistics. These features connect the data model to everyday library operations, rather than presenting isolated screens.

The browser interaction preview demonstrates the catalog, borrowing and returning flow with sample books. The underlying project is a Java application.

items.title: SysChat
items.story:
SysChat is a Python and WebSocket client-server project combining real-time chat with monitoring. The original CV describes CPU, RAM and disk metrics, process management and activity logging.

The technical idea is to bring communication and observability into one interface: clients send and receive messages while operational events remain visible.

The portfolio preview illustrates the two-client message flow with local sample messages. It does not connect to private computers or display real system telemetry.

items.title: Predictive sales analysis
items.description: From 3,636 records to an executive explanation.
items.story:
This Python and Google Colab project worked with 3,636 sales records. The original workflow included data cleaning, variable engineering and multiple linear regression.

Model quality was evaluated through R², mean squared error and root mean squared error. The results were translated into an executive presentation, connecting numerical analysis with a decision-focused explanation.

The interactive view illustrates the relationship between a fitted line and observations using sample values. It does not substitute a new dataset for the original analysis.

items.title: Laguna Hawks
items.description: Engineering stories for a student racing team.
items.story:
Laguna Hawks connects a student gravity-racing project with a public web identity. The website brings together team information, engineering storytelling and sponsorship communication.

It uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript to create a responsive, motion-rich presentation. The work links visual identity with a practical need: helping someone understand the team and the project before deciding how to get involved.

The project also has a newer web direction whose connected team panel is still in development. The public demo here is the established landing-page repository.

items.title: MyFather
items.story:
MyFather organizes biblical learning into Spanish and English lessons, activities and supervised profile flows. Routine lessons and progress do not require AI processing.

Its source documents a one-time completion reward, learning-day logic, distinct adult and child spaces and a public frontend separated from private operations. The interface connects content, progress and account states across the product.

The live website is available from the MacBook as well as the project wall.

items.title: HeForShe · Entre nos
items.description: A warm editorial space for a campus community.
items.story:
Entre nos is an editorial platform developed for the HeForShe community at Tecmilenio Campus Laguna. It brings stories, a digital newspaper, events, educational games and student generations into one warm visual language.

The source includes structured content blocks, publication states, a numbered newspaper archive, events and generation profiles. The editorial workspace separates writing and publishing responsibilities in the connected design.

The portfolio version is the project’s offline demonstration. It uses sample content and local browser storage, rather than real editorial accounts.

items.title: TextHuman Hub
items.description: A collection of code-based file and text utilities.
items.story:
TextHuman Hub is a separate tool collection built around browser-side processing. Its repository contains PDF, image, audio, video, text and developer utilities.

Text and developer tools include JSON formatting, word counting, case conversion, hashes and other deterministic operations. File tools use dedicated libraries rather than a generative model.

The full connected application includes accounts, quota tracking and payments through a Worker and database. This small portfolio preview exposes a few local text utilities, without connecting to paid services.
